clue.text: Ruins components of meal …

definitions.meaning: to dish someone's hopes is to spoil or wreck them, so the verb here means wrecks
the separate courses or plates served at a meal

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a verb meaning wrecks, as in spoiling a chance, and the plural noun for the courses that make up a meal.

clue.text: … melted brie, cut roll and chicken

indicators.note: something melted has lost its shape, so the letters are reshaped into a new order
a cut roll has been trimmed, losing its final letter

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: A recipe step continuing the previous clue: melted brie and a sliced roll served with chicken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims ROLL to ROL; 'melted' rearranges BRIE plus ROL into the answer. The ellipsis ties the surface to the meal in 1 Across.
explanation.definitionFit: A young chicken raised for grilling or roasting is called by this name.

clue.text: Newcastle supporter is so inclined?

parts.note: a pro is someone in favour of something
NE is the postcode area for Newcastle upon Tyne, in north-east England

explanation.surface: A football fan of Newcastle is asked whether they lean a certain way.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful reading: a fan of Newcastle is PRO NE.
explanation.definitionFit: Being disposed or liable to something is the same as being inclined to it.

clue.text: French person shown around capital of Luxembourg

parts.note: something shown or demonstrated has been proven
CA, short for circa, means around a date

indicators.note: the capital, or first letter, of the word that follows is taken

explanation.surface: A French visitor is taken on a tour of Luxembourg's capital city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' looks like a container signal, but here it is CA, circa.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Provence, the region in south-east France, is a French person.

clue.text: Safe blown in explosion, with blooming deadly result?

indicators.note: an explosion scatters pieces, so these letters are blasted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A safecracker's blast goes badly wrong, with deadly consequences.
explanation.definitionFit: Aconite, a poisonous flowering plant, goes by this name, so it is a deadly thing that blooms.

clue.text: Hasten to make hot spicy food, not cold

parts.note: H is the usual abbreviation for hot, as on taps

indicators.note: not means the following letter is left out of the dish

parts.note: curry is a spicy dish
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: Instructions to rush a hot curry, served warm rather than cold.
explanation.definitionFit: To hasten is to move quickly or rush, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Oddly, three kilometre journey

indicators.note: oddly takes the first, third and fifth letters of the word

parts.note: K is the common abbreviation for kilometre

explanation.surface: A walk of exactly three kilometres, strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: A long or arduous journey, especially on foot, is a trek.

clue.text: Seal vault, keeping room safe from the elements

indicators.note: keeping means holding something within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: to stop a hole is to seal it
a vault is an arched roof

explanation.surface: Building advice: seal up the vaulted ceiling so the room stays weatherproof.
explanation.definitionFit: Something built to withstand storms is protected against wind and rain, the elements.

clue.text: Greek course in school near city

parts.note: in, meaning fashionable, is hip
a school of whales or dolphins is also called a pod
Rome is the Italian capital city

explanation.surface: A Greek lesson held in a school beside a city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' suggests a lesson, and 'school' a building; the course is a racecourse.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek track for horse and chariot racing was the hippodrome.

clue.text: Port passed round during dinner, cautiously

indicators.note: passing something round turns it about, so these letters are read backwards
during means the letters sit within the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: At a dinner party the port decanter is circulated with care.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Port' looks like the drink passed round the table; it is the harbour city in Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Acre is a historic harbour city in northern Israel.

clue.text: Vehicle in India or the Friendly Islands

definitions.meaning: a light two-wheeled horse-drawn carriage used in India
the name Captain Cook gave to a Pacific archipelago, now a kingdom

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both an Indian horse-drawn cart and the Pacific kingdom nicknamed the Friendly Islands.

clue.text: Making design of circles in lace work

indicators.note: in means the circles are placed within the lace

parts.note: tatting is a kind of handmade lace
O looks like a circle, so two circles give OO

explanation.surface: Creating a circular pattern in lacework.
explanation.definitionFit: Inking a design into the skin is tattooing, so it is the making of a design.

clue.text: Poor writer takes boat on river

indicators.note: on means placed after, so the boat follows the river in the answer

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement
the Nile is the great African river
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: An impoverished author goes off on a river cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: Having no money at all means being very poor.

clue.text: Plot development that will inevitably surprise theatregoers when introduced

definitions.text: Plot development that will inevitably surprise theatregoers when introduced

parts.words: Plot development that will inevitably surprise theatregoers when introduced
parts.note: an unexpected turn in a story surprises the audience by definition, and the Dickens orphan's surname is introduced to audiences of the musical Oliver!

explanation.walkthrough: A twist is an unexpected turn in a plot, so it always surprises. It is also Oliver's surname, and the musical Oliver! introduces him to theatregoers.
explanation.definitionFit: An unexpected turn in a story is called by this word, and it surprises by its nature.

clue.text: Canned food I had talked of

parts.note: a pie is a common food

indicators.note: talked of means the words are spoken, so the spelling follows the sound

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone describing the tinned food they ate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canned' looks like tinned, with 'food' alongside; it is slang for drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Canned is slang for drunk, and so is this hyphenated word.

clue.text: Dealer rejected single-colour painting?

indicators.note: rejected means thrown back, so the letters are read in reverse

parts.note: a painting all in red could be called red art

explanation.surface: An art dealer turns down a monochrome canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A trader buys and sells goods, so is a dealer.

clue.text: Vehicle fitment daughter installed near Suffolk town, you say?

indicators.note: you say means the town's name is heard, not written

parts.note: Ipswich is the county town of Suffolk, in eastern England

explanation.surface: A car part fitted by a daughter in a garage near Ipswich.
explanation.definitionFit: A car's switch for lowering the headlight beam is a fitment on a vehicle.

clue.text: FBI informer is loading rifle the wrong way, note

indicators.note: the wrong way means back to front, so the combined letters are read backwards
loading means taking on board, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: taken as written
to rifle a place is to loot it
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: An informant is caught loading a gun incorrectly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rifle' looks like a gun being loaded; here it is a verb meaning plunder. 'loading' and 'the wrong way' together make STOOLI.
explanation.definitionFit: Stoolie, short for stool pigeon, is American slang for a police informer.

clue.text: However service comes with 25% off

indicators.note: off means taken away, so the named quarter is removed from the service

parts.note: evensong is the evening church service
a quarter of the eight letters of the church service is its final two

explanation.surface: A church service comes with a quarter-price discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' removes '25%', the last two of EVENSONG's eight letters, NG.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means nevertheless, which is a synonym of however.

clue.text: British individual in pursuit of old American frontiersman

indicators.note: in pursuit of means following behind, so this piece comes after

parts.note: one means a single individual

explanation.surface: A Briton chasing an old American pioneer.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Boone was a famous American pioneer of Kentucky.

clue.text: Exaggerated claim about cases of healthy produce

parts.note: over can mean about, as in arguing over something

indicators.note: the cases are the outer letters that enclose each word

explanation.surface: A marketing boast about the containers of organic vegetables.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cases of' takes the outside letters of both words, H-Y and P-E.
explanation.definitionFit: Excessive promotion or overblown publicity is an exaggerated claim.

clue.text: A group of sailors boarding train in European town

indicators.note: boarding means getting on, so these pieces go inside the train

parts.note: loco is short for locomotive
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Sailors climb aboard a train bound for a European town.
explanation.definitionFit: Locarno is a Swiss town on Lake Maggiore.

clue.text: Recover absolutely, needing energy

indicators.note: needing means lacking, so the letter is taken away

parts.note: really means absolutely or truly
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Getting fully well again requires lots of energy.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally is to recover strength after illness or setback.

clue.text: Dash of liquid served at first with part of meal

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of the word before

parts.note: a platter is a course served on a large dish, as in a seafood platter

explanation.surface: A splash of sauce is served with the opening course.
explanation.definitionFit: A splatter is a splash or spot of liquid.

clue.text: Second in scripture exam? Most unlikely

indicators.note: in means the second piece goes between the others

parts.note: RE is religious education, school scripture lessons
a test is an exam
mo is a moment, a short time

explanation.surface: Coming second in a religious studies test seems very improbable.
explanation.definitionFit: A remotest chance is the slightest, so the word means least likely.

clue.text: Ship being bound for scrap, maybe, with engineers aboard

indicators.note: aboard means on board, so the engineers go inside

parts.note: a fighter is someone heading for a scrap, or fight
RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An old ship destined for the scrapyard with engineers still on board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound for scrap' suggests breaking up a ship; scrap is a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A freighter is a cargo ship.

clue.text: Child came down with scurvy, ultimately? That's all there is to it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
alit means landed or came down

indicators.note: ultimately takes the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A child falls ill with scurvy, and that is the end of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Totality means the whole, the entirety of something.

clue.text: US prison service introducing new form of punishment

parts.note: pen, short for penitentiary, is American for prison

indicators.note: introducing means bringing in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: an ace is an unreturned service in tennis

explanation.surface: An American jail brings in a new way of punishing inmates.
explanation.definitionFit: Penance is self-punishment undertaken to atone for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Check what Homer wrote, for a long time

parts.note: CH is the chess abbreviation for check
the Iliad is Homer's epic poem

explanation.surface: Checking Homer's writing could take ages.
explanation.definitionFit: A chiliad is a thousand years, a very long time.

clue.text: Cook crumble and fish in turn

indicators.note: in turn means turned round, so both pieces are read backwards

parts.note: to rot is to decay or crumble
cod is a fish

explanation.surface: Kitchen instructions: make a crumble and then a fish course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' and 'crumble' look like a dessert recipe; cook means falsify, as in cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To doctor figures is to cook or falsify them.

clue.text: Extra credit will get you first at university

parts.note: top means first or best
UP means in residence at university, as in going up to Oxford

explanation.surface: Coming top at university earns bonus marks.
explanation.definitionFit: A top-up is an additional amount, such as extra phone credit.

clue.text: River boat finally reaching dock, perhaps

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: dock is a common weed, so it is an example of one

explanation.surface: A boat at last reaches its mooring on a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dock' looks like a mooring; it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tweed is a river on the border of England and Scotland.
